Best to avoid Ubuntu.

I always recommend Mint for those transitioning from Windows- just use the default interface, cinnamon. They are honestly not much different.
Check out Elementary OS if you're coming from Mac.
If you want to try a free distro, Trisquel and gNewSense are probably the most beginner-friendly ones.

Both Ubuntu and Mint are very user friendly, in fact Mint is based on Ubuntu (although there is now also a version of Mint based on Debian). There are a few advantages that make me prefer Mint. For example, it comes without the systemd crap, so you don't have to waste time removing that yourself (which might be a little daunting for a beginner).

For someone just transitioning from a Windows or Apple, the more important thing to consider might be the desktop environment you use. Cinnamon and Mate our both similar to the Windows Xp/7 desktop, while Gnome has a layout familiar to Apple users. All of these are available for Mint. The default desktop for Ubuntu is Unity, which I don't find very practical for desktop use (it's more suitable for touch-screens, or maybe small screen laptops). Although you can use other desktops in Ubuntu as well, notably Gnome.

So, in summary, for a Linux newcomer's desktop, go with Mint distro, either Cinnamon, Mate, or Gnome desktop.

You'll get eleven opinions for every ten people you ask, but for myself, I prefer Mint Cinnamon. I don't like the tablet-like desktop experience that Ubuntu's Unity offers, and the Ubuntu team pulled some "big brother" stuff with Unity a few years back that, while they claim to have rolled the changes back, still shake my faith in their motives and ultimately their willingness to keep my data private. Mint Cinnamon offers a polished desktop that is familiar to long-time Windows users, while still offering everything you would expect out of a Debian-based distribution; for me, it's the whole package.
